meta_desc: GCSE Food Technology adventure on Cooking and Food Preparation.
final_note: You worked through the key terms in Cooking and Food Preparation.

concepts.def: Techniques such as boiling, steaming, roasting, grilling and frying, each chosen to suit particular foods and the result required.
The movement of heat into food by conduction, convection and radiation, which underlies how all cooking methods work.
The thickening process in which starch grains absorb liquid and swell when heated, used to thicken sauces such as a roux-based sauce.
The setting of protein when heated, for example egg white turning solid, important in cooking eggs, meat and baked goods.
The browning of sugars when heated to high temperatures, which adds colour and a sweet, rich flavour to foods such as onions.
Planning the order of tasks so that several dishes are prepared efficiently and are ready at the same time when cooking a meal.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Cooking and Food Preparation — a core area of GCSE Food Technology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Cooking and Food Preparation brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Cooking and Food Preparation.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Egg white turning from runny to solid when heated is an example of:
options: Coagulation
Gelatinisation
Caramelisation
Fermentation

mcqs.q: Starch grains swelling and thickening a sauce when heated is called:
options: Gelatinisation
Coagulation
Evaporation
Aeration

mcqs.q: Planning the order of tasks so dishes finish together is known as:
options: Dovetailing
Garnishing
Seasoning
Proving

mcqs.q: The browning of sugar that gives fried onions their flavour is:
options: Caramelisation
Coagulation
Gelatinisation
Oxidation

mcqs.q: What happens during coagulation when an egg is cooked?
options: The egg absorbs water and swells like starch.
The protein in the flour setting solid.
The proteins set, changing the egg from liquid to solid.
The egg releases sugar and browns.

mcqs.q: What causes a starch-based sauce to thicken when heated?
options: The protein in the flour setting solid.
The water evaporating away completely.
The egg releases sugar and browns.
Gelatinisation, as starch grains absorb liquid and swell.

mcqs.q: What is the purpose of 'dovetailing' when cooking a meal?
options: A way of decorating the edges of pastry.
The protein in the flour setting solid.
A method of preserving leftovers.
Organising tasks so several dishes are ready at the same time.
